title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
authors: R. Sennrich, B. Haddow, A. Birch
before: Models had a fixed word vocabulary and an unknown token for everything else.
problem: Rare words, names, morphology and other languages fell outside the vocabulary entirely.
breakthrough: Byte-pair encoding: merge frequent character pairs to build a subword vocabulary that can spell anything.
why: This is why your tokenizer splits words into pieces, and why models count letters badly and handle numbers oddly.
next: WordPiece in GNMT, SentencePiece, and the byte-level BPE in GPT-2 onwards.
inherits: Subword tokenization, still the input layer of essentially every LLM.
